quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards! Their wings beat up to 80 times per second, creating the humming sound that gives them their name. These tiny jewels of the bird world can remember every flower they've visited and how long it will take for the nectar to refill.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Garden Butterflies
short_read.teaser: Discover how butterflies taste with their feet and why they puddle together on wet ground. This charming look at garden visitors reveals their surprising behaviors and how to welcome them to your yard.

medium_read.title: The Ancient Art of Hungarian Embroidery
medium_read.teaser: From the vibrant flowers of Kalocsa to the intricate patterns of Matyó stitching, Hungarian embroidery tells the story of generations. This beautiful tradition continues to inspire artists and preserve cultural memory through needle and thread.

long_read.title: The Wild Olympic Peninsula: A Natural Treasure
long_read.teaser: From ancient rainforests to rocky coastlines, the Olympic Peninsula is one of the most diverse ecosystems in North America. This comprehensive guide explores the plants, animals, and landscapes that make this corner of Washington so extraordinary.

port_angeles.title: Harbor Seal Pupping Season
port_angeles.description: Late August is a wonderful time to spot harbor seal pups along the Strait of Juan de Fuca! These curious youngsters are learning to swim and fish alongside their mothers. Remember to watch from a distance—seals need space to rest and care for their babies.

puzzle_1.question: A baby harbor seal can swim just ___ hours after being born.
puzzle_1.correct_response: That's right, Barbara! These little swimmers are ready to go almost immediately—nature is amazing!
puzzle_1.close_response: Very close! Harbor seal pups can actually swim within about 2 hours of birth. Remarkable little creatures!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Harbor seal pups are ready to swim in just 2 hours! They're born knowing how to swim instinctively.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Harbor seals give birth on land but their pups are born ready for the water. Unlike many mammals, seal pups don't need to learn to swim—they know how from birth!
puzzle_1.learn_more_label: More about harbor seals — NOAA Fisheries

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Beautiful, Barbara! Pillangó is such a lovely word for such a lovely creature!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The word is 'pillangó'—doesn't it sound as delicate as the butterfly itself? (Virág means flower, madár means bird, and kert means garden!)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: The Hungarian word 'pillangó' comes from an old word meaning 'to flutter.' Hungary is home to over 160 species of butterflies, including the stunning Swallowtail.
puzzle_2.learn_more_label: Hungarian nature words — Hungarian for Fun

puzzle_3.question: Which tree is known as the 'nurse log' tree in Olympic rainforests because fallen logs become nurseries for new seedlings?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Wonderful! Sitka Spruce seedlings often grow on fallen logs in the rainforest, creating magical 'colonnades' of trees in a row!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: It's the Sitka Spruce! These trees often grow on 'nurse logs'—fallen trees that provide nutrients and elevation. Eventually the old log decomposes, leaving a colonnade of trees standing in a row like natural columns.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: In the Hoh Rainforest and other Olympic Peninsula forests, you can see rows of Sitka Spruce growing from ancient nurse logs. The young trees benefit from the nutrients and moisture in the decaying wood while staying above the soggy forest floor.
